newsitem.title: USA: Snow, ice for U.S. Midwest ahead of cold weekend.
newsitem.headline: Snow, ice for U.S. Midwest ahead of cold weekend.

text.p: Snow and ice were forecast for much of the U.S. Midwest on Friday, followed by a cold, windy weekend, meteorologists said.

"Tomorrow we'll have a few flurries and it will turn windy and colder," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. "It will be close to zero (degrees Farenheit) Sunday morning in Chicago. Minnesota, Wisconsin and northern Iowa will be well below zero."
The northern Midwest can expect three to six inches of snow by Friday evening. A mix of snow and ice was forecast for Chicago. Points south should see rain and freezing rain.
"The freezing rain is already in Quincy, Ill., Burlington, Iowa and halfway between Moline and Chicago," said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster for Weather Express Inc.
Behind that storm system, temperatures will warm up briefly before dropping sharply below normal Sunday morning, he said.

"The coldest day on the charts is going to be Sunday," he said. "Sunday morning will be -10 to -25 F for spring wheat areas of the Dakotas. That translates for livestock (areas) to maybe zero to -5 across Nebraska."
The 10-day outlook called for unsettled weather about every three days, hitting the Midwest Monday, Thursday and Sunday, Gesser said.
"That will keep the cool air across Canada," Gesser said. "It keeps temperatures below normal across snow covered areas and above normal to the south."
The southern Plains should see moderate temperatures during that period with little chance of precipitation, Weather Services Corp's Burgio said.
"It looks mostly dry," he said. "The only area where they might see some light snow would be Nebraska and Colorado."
He said temperatures would turn a little colder this weekend but "there's no threatening weather in terms of cold for the winter wheat," Burgio said.
